newsitem.title: UK: Dalgety warns of lower second half profits.
newsitem.headline: Dalgety warns of lower second half profits.

text.p: British agro and pet foods company Dalgety Plc warned on Wednesday that a poor third quarter performance for its petfoods and agriculture businesses would affect its second-half performance.
The company said in a statement its dividend would be reduced by one third to restore cover.
"The final dividend is expected to be not less than six pence, to make the total for the year not less than 14.5p (22p)," the company said.
The company cited production difficulties in petfoods, the prolonged impact of BSE on agriculture and the strength of sterling as main reasons for the expected dismal performance.
The company is implementing management changes which include the step-down of Nigel Garrow as chief executive of Petfoods and from the board of Dalgety Plc.
Hugh Donaldson has been appointed the new chief executive with immediate effect, the company said.
Dalgety said it expects to incur exceptional costs of 36 million stg in its current year's results.
The company's cost reduction measures for petfoods will alone cost 27 million stg. The continued impact of BSE has enforced an asset write-down of about nine million stg.

"The continued underperformance of our petfoods business has led us to conclude that tough action is required to ensure that we are on track to meet our financial objectives, albeit late," said Denys Henderson, chairman of Dalgety.
BSE's pressure on cattlefood has remained with sales dipping 25 to 30 percent below the previous year.
The company plans to reduce further capacity in cattlefood which would cost about six million stg, eventually producing annual savings of about two million stg.
Henderson said henceforth he would be working closely with Donaldson, group chief executive Richard Clothier and finance director Ken Hanna to help correct the division's performance.
